04d44b18-6068-486d-afc5-f87f1dd28766.name: Bachelor of Business
04d44b18-6068-486d-afc5-f87f1dd28766.description: The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Business is a 72 credit point degree built around a shared core of introductory management, economics, politics, law and professional skills units, on top of which students choose one specialist major from Marketing, Human Resource Management, International Business, Accounting, Accounting and Finance, Government, Business Economics or Management. The remaining 24 credit points are open electives, which can be taken as a further breadth major, a minor, or individual units from anywhere in the university. The course is offered on campus and in blended delivery, and is based at UC's Bruce campus in Canberra, close to the federal public service and the ACT's business community.
04d44b18-6068-486d-afc5-f87f1dd28766.curriculum:
Core Major in Business (24 credit points): Introduction to Management (11174); Introduction to Economics (11175); Business Law (11220) and related foundation units; professional orientation and evidence units.
Specialist Major (24 credit points, choose 1 of 8): Marketing (SM0025); Human Resource Management (SM0022); International Business (SM0023); Accounting (SM0016, 24/33/39cp options); Accounting and Finance; Government; Business Economics; Management.
Open Electives (24 credit points): from anywhere in the university, as a breadth major, breadth minor, or individual units; at least 18 credit points overall must be at Level 3 or above.
04d44b18-6068-486d-afc5-f87f1dd28766.admission_requirements: Admission is based on an entrance rank, achieved via a Year 12 ATAR, another Australian qualification, relevant work experience, or an overseas qualification equivalent. No assumed knowledge is required.
04d44b18-6068-486d-afc5-f87f1dd28766.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.0 overall, with no band score below 6.0 (or equivalent).

32c97e56-5b56-4328-aa9b-6026a34eec1b.name: Bachelor of Government
32c97e56-5b56-4328-aa9b-6026a34eec1b.admission_requirements: Admission is based on an entrance rank, achieved via a Year 12 ATAR, another Australian qualification, relevant work experience, or an overseas qualification equivalent. No assumed knowledge is required.
32c97e56-5b56-4328-aa9b-6026a34eec1b.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.0 overall, with no band score below 6.0 (or equivalent).
32c97e56-5b56-4328-aa9b-6026a34eec1b.curriculum:
Core Major in Government (24 credit points): Introduction to Management (11174); Introduction to Economics (11175); Introduction to Politics and Government (11235); Professional Evidence (Government and Policy) (11237); Law and Society (11257); Professional Orientation (Business, Government and Law) (12209); plus a restricted choice covering Investigating and Explaining Society or Quantitative Methods, and a professional/internship option (BGL Internship A to D, or an International Business Study Tour).
Specialist Major (24 credit points, choose 1 of 3): Politics and International Relations (SM0030), covering units such as Introduction to International Relations, National Security, Foreign Policy and Geopolitics; Applied Economics (SM0093), covering units such as Public Sector Economics, Managing the Economy and Econometrics; Public Policy and Administration (SM0094), covering units such as Introduction to Public Policy, How Government Works and Public Sector Performance Management.
Open Electives (24 credit points): from anywhere in the university, as a breadth major, breadth minor and/or individual units.

f24eb416-85e8-400d-bc67-b66626c5a3eb.name: Bachelor of Information Technology
f24eb416-85e8-400d-bc67-b66626c5a3eb.admission_requirements: Admission is based on an entrance rank, achieved via a Year 12 ATAR, another Australian qualification, relevant work experience, or an overseas qualification equivalent, plus alternative-entry pathway options. Assumed knowledge: basic ICT skills and basic numeracy and literacy.
f24eb416-85e8-400d-bc67-b66626c5a3eb.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.0 overall, with no band score below 6.0 (or equivalent).
f24eb416-85e8-400d-bc67-b66626c5a3eb.curriculum:
Core Major in Information Technology and Systems (24 credit points): Introduction to Information Technology (4478); Database Design (5915); Professional Practice in IT (7722); Information & Communication Technology Project (9785); Technological Innovation and Entrepreneurship (11408); Systems Analysis and Modelling (11486); plus Introduction to Network Engineering (11485).
Specialist Major in Information Technology (24 credit points): Software Technology 1 (4483); Designing Human-Computer Interaction (6389); Discrete Mathematics (6698); Systems Project and Quality Management (7173); Web Design and Programming (7175); Enterprise and Cloud Computing (9281); Software Systems Architecture (11491); plus an Information Security unit.
One further specialist stream (24 credit points, choose 1 of 4): Robotics and AI (SM0058), covering units such as Foundations of Robotics, Computer Vision and Image Analysis, and Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning; Cybersecurity and System Administration (SM0056), covering units such as Introduction to Digital Forensics, Network Architecture and System and Network Administration; Data Science; or Cloud Computing and IoT.
High-achieving graduates can progress to a one-year Honours program in the ITS discipline.

671ef8a9-db83-4416-a0de-967ac29bfcba.name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
671ef8a9-db83-4416-a0de-967ac29bfcba.admission_requirements: Admission is based on an entrance rank, achieved via a Year 12 ATAR, another Australian qualification, relevant work experience, or an overseas qualification equivalent, plus alternative-entry pathway options. For Work Integrated Learning placements, students may require a police check, a Working with Vulnerable People card, and current vaccinations. Assumed knowledge (ACT): Biology, Mathematical Methods; (NSW): Biology, Mathematics.
671ef8a9-db83-4416-a0de-967ac29bfcba.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.0 overall, with no band score below 6.0 (or equivalent).
671ef8a9-db83-4416-a0de-967ac29bfcba.curriculum:
Specialist Major in Human Movement (24 credit points): Biomechanics 1 and 2 (6834, 6835); Advanced Functional Anatomy (8279); Human Growth and Development (8338); Physiology of Exercise 1 and 2 (8391, 8392); plus an Exercise Programming and Prescription unit.
Core Major in Allied Health (24 credit points): Systemic Anatomy and Physiology (6529); Regional Anatomy and Physiology (9808); Introduction to Research in the Health Sciences (11398); Understanding People and Behaviour (11399); Professional Orientation (Health) (11400); plus a capstone research or practicum sequence (Exercise Science Practicum and Exercise Science Capstone, or Research and Professional Practice Parts A and B).
Remaining credit points: open electives.
Students complete 140 hours of Work Integrated Learning placement, including opportunities through UC's Student-Led Clinic and professional partners such as the Canberra Raiders, ACT Brumbies, Canberra United and UC Capitals. On completion, graduates can apply for accreditation with Exercise & Sports Science Australia (ESSA) as an Accredited Exercise Scientist.

4107cafc-bbac-4eb0-8a3f-448858f2717b.name: Bachelor of Secondary Education
4107cafc-bbac-4eb0-8a3f-448858f2717b.curriculum: UC does not offer a single generic 'Bachelor of Secondary Education' course of its own; students enrol in one of its specialisation-coded variants (for example Arts 347JA, Science 348JA, or Health and Physical Education 330JA), each of which shares the same core professional-teaching sequence but differs in its subject-area major. Shared core units (drawn from the Arts variant, 347JA) include Foundations of Pedagogy (11765); Being a Teacher (12034); Core Literacy (9863); Educational Investigations (9870); Teachers as Professionals (9918); Using Data to Improve Learning (10354); and Engaging with LANTITE (10453), a zero-credit unit that tracks completion of the national Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education students. Students then complete Teaching Secondary Discipline Methods units matched to their two chosen teaching areas (for example Teaching Secondary English, Teaching Secondary Humanities and Social Sciences, or Teaching Secondary Technologies), plus a 36 credit point disciplinary major in each teaching area, defined against the NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA) Subject Content Requirements. All variants include a minimum of 80 days of professional placement across different secondary settings, ending in a 30-day placement in the final year.

e2ff3d37-f838-4e6d-b401-d15fa066b4e6.name: Master of Information Technology
e2ff3d37-f838-4e6d-b401-d15fa066b4e6.admission_requirements: An Australian bachelor degree in any field, or equivalent. Applicants with significant relevant work experience or industry-recognised qualifications may also enter via UC's Professional Pathway Entry program. Assumed knowledge: proficiency in using computers.
e2ff3d37-f838-4e6d-b401-d15fa066b4e6.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.5 overall, with no band score below 6.0 (or equivalent).
